Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

summary noun

also abstract (summary), synopsis, précis, abridgment, in summary, to sum up, in short, briefly

classical

Sen. Ep. 39.1 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 387

summārium, summāriī n.

noun, second declension

a summary, an abstract

From summa, the main points. Seneca says it was the Latin word, and breviārium the one people used in his day.

Other words

  • epitomē, epitomēs f. — an abridgment, an epitome (of a book)

    noun · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.5.3; 13.8 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. summary

    A Greek word, used by Cicero of a shortened version of a longer work; also epitoma, epitomae f. (Cic. Att. 12.5.3).

  • breviārium, breviāriī n. — a summary, an abstract

    noun, second declension · also used · post-classical · Sen. Ep. 39.1; Suet. (Lewis & Short, s.v. breviārius); Traupman 387

    Post-Augustan; the everyday word of Seneca’s time, by his own account.

  • summātim — briefly, in summary

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.16.1: aliquid summātim perscrībere; Varr. RR 2 praef. 6: breviter ac summātim percurram (Lewis & Short)

    To give the gist: summātim nārrāre, perscrībere.

  • ad summam — in short, to sum up

    adverbial phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 14.1.1; Off. 1.149 (Lewis & Short, s.v. summa)

    “In a word”, closing a list or an argument.

Examples

  • ōrātiō, quae nunc vulgō breviārium dīcitur, ōlim, cum Latīnē loquerēmur, summārium vocābātur

    the kind of piece now commonly called a breviarium was once, when we spoke Latin, called a summariumSen. Ep. 39.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • Ita vīdistī summātim rēs omnēs, quae ostendī poterunt

    So you have seen, in brief, all the things that could be shownComen. OP, Clausula

See also describe, CV.
